name: RoguePlanet â€” Microsoft Defender Privilege Escalation Zero-Day
description: RoguePlanet is a Windows local privilege escalation zero-day publicly released on June 9, 2026 by the pseudonymous researcher 'Nightmare Eclipse' (aka Chaotic Eclipse), just hours after that month's Patch Tuesday. It exploits a race condition in Microsoft Defender's handling of the 'mpengine!SysIO*' API family, allowing an unprivileged local user to spawn a SYSTEM-level command prompt â€” success has been validated as 100% on some machines but inconsistent on others. The exploit was originally developed as a remote code execution chain abusing Defender's handling of files on remote SMB shares and VHD/VHDX mounts (and could bypass BitLocker), but Microsoft hardened that path in mid-May 2026, forcing a rewrite into the current local privilege escalation variant. Confirmed to work against Windows 10 with June 2026 updates and Windows 11 (Official and Canary builds, including KB5094126); it does not function on Windows Server, though the researcher believes server builds are also vulnerable. RoguePlanet is the latest in Nightmare Eclipse's ongoing disclosure spree against Microsoft Defender â€” following BlueHammer, RedSun, GreenPlasma, and YellowKey â€” driven by the researcher's frustration with Microsoft's vulnerability disclosure and bug-bounty practices. After GitHub and GitLab removed prior repositories, the PoC was published on a self-hosted git instance (projectnightcrawler.dev).

detection_opportunities: Monitor for unexpected SYSTEM-privileged cmd.exe or process creation originating from MsMpEng.exe (Defender's engine process)
Watch for rapid, race-condition-style file operation sequences targeting paths handled by mpengine!SysIO* APIs
Track Microsoft's security advisories and CISA KEV for a forthcoming CVE and patch addressing this Defender race condition
